title: Tax-refund "claim" link vs. bank note on a failed refund-account validation
summary: A caller from Kaveri Bank phones about the recipient's pending income-tax refund. In the fraud case, the caller says the refund is stuck, sends a link to "claim" it, and asks the recipient to enter their debit card number, CVV, and the OTP that follows. In the legitimate case, the caller says the tax portal's request to validate the recipient's Kaveri Bank account for refunds failed because the name on the account does not match. The recipient is asked to correct the name at a branch and then re-validate on the official tax portal themselves.

shared_setting.pretext: the recipient filed an income-tax return and is expecting a refund of about [AMOUNT_1] (₹2,000–₹60,000).
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult salaried or self-employed taxpayer; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers say the refund "cannot be credited yet" and needs "validation".

fraud.label_rationale: The caller directs the recipient to an unofficial link and asks for card credentials and an OTP to receive a refund. Receiving a refund never needs card details or an OTP.
fraud.caller_objective: Capture the recipient's debit card number, CVV, and the OTP that authorises a payment.
stable_facts: Link: https://kaveri-taxrefund-claim.invalid/validate (sent by SMS during the call).
The caller says the refund "expires" if not claimed within 24 hours.
The page asks for card number, expiry, CVV, and then the OTP.

evidence.text: Caller tells the recipient to open the link and enter their debit card number and CVV to claim the refund
Caller says the refund will lapse within 24 hours

legitimate.label_rationale: The caller explains a real validation problem, tells the recipient how to fix it at the branch, and leaves the tax-portal step to the recipient. No link, card detail, or OTP is requested.
legitimate.caller_objective: Get the recipient to correct the account name so the refund account validates.
stable_facts: The tax portal's validation request for this account was rejected because the account name differs from the name on the recipient's PAN (for example, a missing middle name).
Fix: visit any Kaveri Bank branch with PAN and ID to correct the name, then re-validate the account on the official tax portal by typing its address themselves.
The refund is credited only after validation succeeds. The caller does not say how long that takes or give any deadline.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may insist on the link, resend it, or raise urgency. They must not switch to a different mechanism (for example a payment to a UPI ID or an app install). The legitimate caller must not send a link or ask for any credential after the branch.

must_preserve: refund amount and "cannot be credited yet" in both
name-mismatch reason, branch fix, and self-typed portal (_L)
may_vary: up to 2 filler turns before turn 3
must_not_emit: real tax-portal URLs or e-mail addresses
real PAN formats beyond a placeholder

ambiguities: The catalog's legitimate case ("bank says refund credited, no action needed") gave the caller no reason to call and no parallel to the "validation" pretext. This card uses a failed account validation instead.
Banks do not usually phone customers about tax-portal validation; they may send an SMS. The call is a simplification for pairing, and reviewers should decide whether it is plausible enough.
Whether a pending refund can lapse was not verified. The legitimate caller must not make claims about refund deadlines.
Validation" and "refund" appear in both cases. The label depends on the link and the card-detail request.

evidence_references.claim: Refunds are credited only to a bank account pre-validated on the e-filing portal (CB20)
The Income Tax Department does not ask by e-mail for PINs or passwords (CB19)
Banks and genuine entities never ask for card details, CVV, or OTP (C01)
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
